title: The Corridor and the Symbol: an Engineer Brings Urbanism to Argentina
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the builder's house
stops.date_confidence: attested for 7 September 1890 by es.wikipedia and by Infobae (16 November 2022), which also gives the parents. No street address of the birth was found in any source reached, so the pin is the canonical Buenos Aires point already carried in this atlas rather than a documented house
stops.campa: A son is born to Cayetano della Paolera, a builder, and to Ángela Buschiazzo, kin of Juan Antonio Buschiazzo, the architect the municipality calls when it wants a cemetery laid out or an avenue drawn. The house is trade on one side and drawing board on the other. Outside it a city is doubling every fifteen years on immigration and beef, filling a colonial grid nobody designed for a million people, and the corridor its intendentes keep sketching for one great central avenue is already a year older than the child. No source gives the street.
suggested_refs: The municipal works of Juan Antonio Buschiazzo, the mother's kinsman, in the Buenos Aires of the 1890s
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio: un ancho increíble, un obelisco por una fuente y el sueño de su creador' (16 November 2022)

stops.name: Colegio Nacional de Buenos Aires, the elite secondary
stops.date_confidence: the attendance is attested by Infobae (16 November 2022); the previous dossier carried it as unverified tradition and that tag is lifted here. No year is given by any source, so 1903 is an ordering device derived from the birth date and nothing more, with month and day defaulted to 01. Coordinates corrected: OSM/Nominatim places the Colegio at Moreno and Bolívar, some 215 m from the pair the dossier carried
stops.campa: He is put into the Colegio Nacional, the school bolted to the university and to the governing class that passes through it, three blocks from the Plaza de Mayo in the old Jesuit quarter. Latin, mathematics, the sons of ministers at the next desk. The building stands inside the Manzana de las Luces, the block that has held the colonial university, the printing press, and tunnels nobody has mapped. He will spend most of his working life within a kilometre of this corner. No school register of his years here has been located.
suggested_refs: The registers of the Colegio Nacional de Buenos Aires for the first decade of the century, not consulted for this journey
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio...' (16 November 2022)
OpenStreetMap/Nominatim, Colegio Nacional de Buenos Aires, Monserrat

stops.name: Manzana de las Luces, water for a hundred thousand
stops.date_confidence: the civil engineering degree from the Universidad de Buenos Aires in 1912 is attested by Infobae (16 November 2022). The exact date of 19 November and the thesis title are dossier-only and unverified. A direct contradiction is left standing: es.wikipedia states he began his engineering studies in 1912, which cannot be reconciled with graduation in the same year, and the studies must therefore have begun around 1907 or 1908. Coordinates corrected to the OSM figure for the Manzana de las Luces, some 370 m from the dossier's pair
stops.campa: He graduates civil engineer from the University of Buenos Aires with a thesis on the provision of water for a city of a hundred thousand inhabitants: how to bring water to a place that does not yet exist, sized in advance. The problem is one of supply and not of appearance, and the later work keeps that order, taking pipes, rails and traffic before facades. He is twenty-two. In the same year, and with no connection to him, a national law authorises the expropriation of a corridor through the centre of Buenos Aires for an avenue thirty-three metres wide.
suggested_refs: National Law 8,855 of 1912, authorising expropriation of the Cerrito to Bernardo de Irigoyen corridor
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio...' (16 November 2022)
OpenStreetMap/Nominatim, Manzana de las Luces, Perú 294

stops.name: Centro Argentino de Ingenieros, the Congreso de la Habitación
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The delegation to the Congreso de la Habitación convened by the Museo Social Argentino is carried by the dossier alone and was corroborated by no source fetched; month and day default to 01. Coordinates corrected: OSM gives the Centro Argentino de Ingenieros at Cerrito 1250 some 700 m from the pair the dossier carried
stops.campa: Eight years an engineer, he is sent by the Centro Argentino de Ingenieros as its delegate to a congress on housing convened by the Museo Social Argentino. Housing is where Argentine engineering meets the social question: conventillos, tuberculosis, the arithmetic of rent against wage. The profession that trained him to size a water main is being asked what a city owes the people living inside it. No proceedings of the congress were reached, and what he said in them is not known. Within a year he has left for Paris to study urbanismo, a subject no Argentine university teaches.
suggested_refs: The proceedings of the Congreso de la Habitación, Museo Social Argentino, Buenos Aires 1920
sources: OpenStreetMap/Nominatim, Centro Argentino de Ingenieros, Cerrito 1250

stops.name: Paris, the Institut d'Urbanisme and Marcel Poëte
stops.date_confidence: the 1921 to 1928 span at the IUUP under Marcel Poëte is attested by journals.openedition.org/abe/10839; month and day default to 01. Some institutional biographies place the decisive move in 1924 instead, and that discrepancy is not resolved here. The pin is the canonical central Paris point carried across this atlas rather than the institute's own address, which was not confirmed
stops.campa: He enrols at the Institut d'Urbanisme de l'Université de Paris, founded three years earlier, and attaches himself to Marcel Poëte, historian of cities, who teaches that a city is read before it is drawn: its old plans, its ground, its growth curves, the accumulated evidence of what it has already been. The method is diagnostic and historical, and it is the opposite of beginning from a blank sheet. Buenos Aires, at this distance, becomes the city he practises the reading on. He stays seven years.
suggested_refs: The Poëte fonds in the Bibliothèque historique de la Ville de Paris, which holds correspondence between master and student

stops.name: Amsterdam, the Beurs van Berlage
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Both the attendance and the venue come from the dossier alone; neither was corroborated by any source fetched, and the day defaults to 01. The Beurs van Berlage is a best guess at the congress hall and should be treated as such
stops.campa: The Centro Argentino de Ingenieros sends him north to an international city-planning congress in Amsterdam, into the argument Europe is having with itself about the garden city, the extension plan and the regional survey. The Dutch have been planning municipal extensions by statute since 1901; Argentina has no such law, and nobody at home qualified to draft one. The hall is said to be Berlage's exchange building on the Damrak, brick and iron and deliberately severe, twenty years old and already a monument.
suggested_refs: The Dutch Housing Act of 1901 and the statutory extension plan, the model under discussion at Amsterdam

stops.name: Paris, a French household
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction throughout. The marriage to Marie Thérèse Rouault and the birth of Carlos María José della Paolera Rouault on 25 March 1926 come from user-contributed genealogies relayed by the dossier, which itself flags them as provisional. No marriage certificate and no birth record were located
stops.campa: He marries Marie Thérèse Rouault, met, the family account holds, during the study years, and in March a first son is born in Paris and registered Carlos María José della Paolera Rouault. The Argentine engineer has become a Parisian householder with a thesis unfinished and a French wife, in the years when the Buenos Aires he writes about is being planned at home by a commission he has no part in. The genealogy is family-supplied and rests on nothing archival.
suggested_refs: Paris civil registers for 1926, not consulted for this journey
sources: Web crawl dossier, drawn from user-contributed genealogies

stops.name: Paris, the articles written for La Razón
stops.date_confidence: the quoted article is attested: La Razón, 14 April 1927, quoted with full citation in Alicia Novick, 'Planes versus proyectos', Revista de Urbanismo N°3 (2000), p.15, a PDF read directly for this journey. The wider series of articles on the city's lungs and its monumental ensembles is dossier-only. The physical location of writing is Paris; publication was in Buenos Aires, and the pin follows the writer
stops.campa: He writes to Buenos Aires from Paris, a run of articles in La Razón on the lungs of the city, its monumental ensembles, and a regulatory plan for the whole agglomeration rather than the municipality alone. Two years earlier the Noel commission at home, with Jean-Claude Nicolas Forestier advising, had published exactly the sort of beautiful document he is writing against. In April he sets out the distinction the rest of his career rests on. A plano is a drawing, agreeably coloured, showing everything projected for a city. A plan regulador is an instrument.
stops.quote: una representación gráfica, agradablemente coloreada, en la que figuran todas las transformaciones proyectadas para una ciudad existente o todas las estructuras previstas para una ciudad a crearse
stops.quote_source: Carlos María della Paolera, 'El Plan Regulador de la Aglomeración Bonaerense. 1. La Capital y las zonas edificadas exteriores a su jurisdicción', La Razón, 14 April 1927, quoted in Alicia Novick, 'Planes versus proyectos', Revista de Urbanismo N°3 (2000), p.15
suggested_refs: Proyecto Orgánico para la urbanización del municipio, Buenos Aires 1925, the Noel commission plan he is arguing against
sources: Alicia Novick, 'Planes versus proyectos: algunos problemas constitutivos del Urbanismo Moderno. Buenos Aires (1910-1936)', Revista de Urbanismo N°3 (2000)
Web crawl dossier for the wider article series

stops.name: Brussels, speaking for a continent
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The representation of South America at the Union Internationale des Villes is a dossier claim corroborated by nothing fetched; month and day default to 01, and the Grand Place town hall is a landmark standing in for an institutional seat that was not established
stops.campa: He represents South America at the Union Internationale des Villes, the municipal federation founded at Ghent in 1913 so that cities could speak to each other over the heads of their states. A continent of twenty republics is spoken for by one Argentine engineer who has never held a municipal post anywhere, in a body whose members are mayors and municipal technicians with budgets behind them. The credential he carries into the room is a Paris diploma and a set of newspaper articles. What he said there has not been found, and the union's seat in these years is not established by any source reached.
suggested_refs: The bulletins of the Union Internationale des Villes for the late 1920s

stops.name: Paris, the diploma thesis defended
stops.date_confidence: the thesis, its title, its supervisor and the year 1928 are attested by redalyc.org/journal/1251/125162706005/html/ and by journals.openedition.org/abe/10839. The exact defence date of 31 March is dossier-only and was not reconfirmed. The claim that he was the first Latin American to take the institute's diploma rests on the dossier and on institutional biographies, not on the institute's own register
stops.campa: He defends his diploma thesis under Poëte: Contribution à l'étude d'un plan d'aménagement, d'embellissement et d'extension de Buenos Aires. It is his own city, studied at seven thousand miles by the historical method of a French school. He has been away the better part of a decade, and what he carries home is a method. By the accounts that circulate afterwards he is the first Latin American to take the institute's urbanism diploma; those accounts are institutional biographies, and the institute's own register has not been checked.
suggested_refs: Contribution à l'étude d'un plan d'aménagement, d'embellissement et d'extension de Buenos Aires, IUUP diploma thesis, 1928

segments.name: The Return: Buenos Aires and Rosario

stops.name: Manzana de las Luces, ten lectures on the evolution of a city
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The lecture series and its title are dossier-only; the venue within the university was not verified, and the day defaults to 01. That he was advocating comprehensive metropolitan planning for Buenos Aires from 1928 is separately attested by es.wikipedia's article on the Avenida 9 de Julio
stops.campa: Back in Buenos Aires he delivers ten lectures under the title La evolución de Buenos Aires y bosquejo de un Plan Regulador: the city's growth traced forward from the colonial grid, and only then a sketch of what should follow from it. The sequence is Poëte's, evidence before proposal, and he has to teach the sequence before he can use it: there is not yet a chair of urbanism anywhere in the country he is lecturing in. Which room in the university he spoke in has not been verified. He is thirty-seven and employed by no municipality.
suggested_refs: The surviving text of La evolución de Buenos Aires y bosquejo de un Plan Regulador, ten lectures of 1928

stops.name: Rosario, two conferences at Ángel Guido's invitation
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the visit and the pamphlet, both dossier-only. What is independently confirmed is only that a professional relationship with Ángel Guido existed by 1929, per the Scielo article on the Rosario plan. Month and day default to 01. The pin is Plaza 25 de Mayo, the city's civic centre and the reference point of the later plan, not a documented lecture hall
stops.campa: The architect Ángel Guido, who is building a Rosario of his own and arguing for an American architecture rooted in the pre-Columbian Andes, brings him up the Paraná to lecture. Rosario is the second city, a grain port grown vertiginously on railways it does not own, its waterfront handed over to companies and its centre thickening without a plan. He will be working on this city for the next six years. The two lectures are printed as a pamphlet: Dos conferencias sobre urbanismo. Rosario y sus problemas urbanos.
suggested_refs: Dos conferencias sobre urbanismo. Rosario y sus problemas urbanos, printed pamphlet

stops.name: Rosario, the first chair of urbanism in Argentina
stops.date_confidence: the year 1929 and the institutional fact are attested twice over: vitruvius.com.br arquitextos 08.087/216 and iaa.fadu.uba.ar/ojs article 264. The dossier's precise date of 31 December is dropped as unsupported, and month and day default to 01. The pin is the Rosario architecture school at Riobamba 220 bis rather than the city centre, and is approximate
stops.campa: The Universidad Nacional del Litoral creates in its Rosario architecture school the first university chair of urbanism in Argentina, and gives it to him. For the students in front of him the word urbanismo has existed in Spanish about a decade, and the man using it holds a Paris diploma in it. The discipline enters the country as a teaching post before it enters it as an office or a law. He travels three hundred kilometres up the river from Buenos Aires to hold the post, and goes on doing it for years.
suggested_refs: The founding programme of the urbanism chair, Universidad Nacional del Litoral, Rosario, 1929

stops.name: Rosario, Ordinance 58 and the commission
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1929 by scielo.org.ar/scielo.php?pid=S2314-15492016000100003, which names Municipal Ordinance No. 58, the two collaborators, the twenty-kilometre radius from Plaza 25 de Mayo and the 1935 approval; month and day default to 01. The local objection to a direct appointment made without open competition is carried by the same tradition and is not a matter of any legal finding
stops.campa: Municipal Ordinance 58 commissions him, with Ángel Guido and the engineer Adolfo Farengo, to draw a Plan Regulador y de Extensión for Rosario. There is no competition; the appointment is direct, and the local profession says so loudly. What the three propose is regional before it is municipal: the railways reorganised, the port restructured, open ground reserved, the whole read inside a radius of twenty kilometres struck from Plaza 25 de Mayo. Six years pass before the council approves it.
suggested_refs: Ordenanza Municipal N°58, Rosario, 1929

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the season city
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The lectures at Mar del Plata in 1931 or 1932 are dossier-only, the venue unconfirmed, and no evidence was found that the municipality adopted a plan from him. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: He lectures on the coast, at the resort the Buenos Aires bourgeoisie built for its summers: a city that triples in January and empties in March, extending along the sea in lots without reserving anything between them. The hall he spoke in has not been identified, and nothing reached shows Mar del Plata adopting a plan from him. His argument is the garden-city argument applied to a place that is all frontage: open ground has to be taken before the land is sold, never after it.
suggested_refs: The Rambla and the seasonal expansion of Mar del Plata in the 1930s

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Werner Hegemann comes through
stops.date_confidence: split evidence. Hegemann's 1931 South American lecture tour and his Mar del Plata appearance are attested by en.wikipedia.org, 'Werner Hegemann'. Della Paolera's chairing of the hosting committee, the Buenos Aires and Rosario legs of the itinerary, and his prologue to Problemas urbanos de Rosario are all dossier-only and uncorroborated. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: Werner Hegemann, driven out of Germany's argument with itself about the city and touring South America, comes through Argentina lecturing on civic art and on the plan as a social instrument. The committee that receives him is said to be della Paolera's, and the itinerary said to run Buenos Aires, Rosario, Mar del Plata, the exact circuit of his own work. The tour is documented. His part in hosting it is not, and neither is the prologue he is said to have written for Hegemann's book on Rosario.
suggested_refs: Werner Hegemann, Problemas urbanos de Rosario, Spanish edition, with a prologue attributed to della Paolera
sources: Web crawl dossier for della Paolera's role

segments.name: The Office, the Chair, the Symbol

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Dirección del Plan de Urbanización
stops.date_confidence: the appointment and the year 1932 are attested by journals.openedition.org/abe/10839, which also gives the pressure from a socialist group on the city council, and are corroborated by Infobae. The precise ordinance date of 5 February is dossier-only. The end of the tenure is a live contradiction: es.wikipedia gives 1939, Novick and Piccioni give 1943, and neither can be preferred on the evidence gathered. No street address for the office survives, so the pin is the canonical city point
stops.campa: The municipality creates a technical office for the plan of urbanisation and puts him at the head of it, after pressure from the socialist bloc on the city council. It is the first sustained planning office Buenos Aires has had: not a commission convened to produce a document and then dissolve, but a standing desk inside the administration with a director who means to stay at it. He is forty-one. How long he stays is disputed: one account ends the tenure in 1939 and another in 1943, and nothing gathered here decides between them.
suggested_refs: Alicia Novick and Hortensia Piccioni on the Oficina del Plan de Urbanización and its tenure
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio...' (16 November 2022)

stops.name: Manzana de las Luces, the chair at Buenos Aires
stops.date_confidence: the year 1933 is attested by vitruvius.com.br arquitextos 08.087/216; the dossier's date of 25 May is dropped as unsupported and month and day default to 01. The place has been corrected for anachronism: the University of Buenos Aires had no faculty of architecture in 1933, architecture being taught inside the Facultad de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales, and the Facultad de Arquitectura y Urbanismo was created only in 1948. His criticism of Le Corbusier's tabula rasa is documented in the dossier and is not tied there to any dated text
stops.campa: A second chair of urbanism, this one at the University of Buenos Aires, where architecture is still taught inside the faculty of exact, physical and natural sciences and will not have a faculty of its own for fifteen years. He now teaches in two cities and directs an office in one of them. What he teaches against by name is the proposal to clear the ground and begin again: Le Corbusier had lectured in this city in 1929 and printed the lectures as Précisions, and the blank sheet is precisely what Poëte's method forbids.
suggested_refs: Le Corbusier, Précisions sur un état présent de l'architecture et de l'urbanisme (1930), the Buenos Aires lectures of October 1929
sources: Web crawl dossier for the criticism of Le Corbusier

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Manifiesto del Símbolo del Urbanismo
stops.date_confidence: the manifesto is dated November 1934 by the text as reproduced online; no archival or scholarly edition of it was locatable, and the quotation below is taken from a 2013 reproduction on a Peruvian urbanism blog, cited in turn by an academic article whose own note points back to the same page, so the chain is single-rooted. The commonly circulated variant punctuates it as La ciudad, como el árbol, and that repunctuation is not in the reproduced text. Day defaults to 01
stops.campa: He publishes a manifesto and a device to go with it: a symbol of urbanism, sun and vegetation and air compressed into one mark, meant to be legible to a profession scattered across languages and continents. The argument inside it is organicist and old: no amount of technique releases a city from the ground it stands on. No archival or scholarly edition of the text has been located, and its wording reaches the present through a single reproduction posted online in 2013. The thing itself is a piece of insignia, sun and greenery and sky in one mark, the least engineering-like object he ever makes.
stops.quote: La ciencia urbanística ha puesto plenamente en evidencia que la utilización en la ciudad de los mas maravillosos e inesperados recursos de la técnica no debe ni puede excluir el aprovechamiento intensivo de los elementos naturales. La ciudad como el árbol no puede desligarse de la tierra que la sustenta.
stops.quote_source: Manifiesto del Símbolo del Urbanismo, noviembre de 1934, as reproduced at surp-aqp.blogspot.com (2013) and cited in João Soares Pena, 'Dia Mundial do Urbanismo', Arquitextos 186.08, Vitruvius (2015); the manifesto itself was not consulted
suggested_refs: The 1934 Símbolo del Urbanismo, sun, greenery and sky in a single device

stops.name: Besançon, the congress adopts the mark
stops.date_confidence: attested by vitruvius.com.br arquitextos 08.087/216, which states that the symbol of urbanism was adopted by the Congress of Urbanism of 1935 and that the eighth of November was established there as the day of urbanism. What is not established by anything reached is whether della Paolera travelled to Besançon in person or the symbol was adopted in his absence, and that caveat is kept. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: The congress of urbanism meeting at Besançon adopts the symbol and fixes the eighth of November as a day for the discipline. Besançon is a garrison town in the Doubs, walled by Vauban, the sort of place where European planners meet each other away from capitals. A device drawn in Buenos Aires for a profession that barely exists there is taken up in eastern France and given a place on the calendar. Whether the Argentine who made the mark is in the room, nothing reached will say.
suggested_refs: The proceedings of the 1935 Congrès d'Urbanisme at Besançon

stops.name: Rosario, the plan approved
stops.date_confidence: the 1935 approval is attested by scielo.org.ar/scielo.php?pid=S2314-15492016000100003; month and day default to 01. The quoted sentences come from the plan's own Memoria descriptiva y justificativa (Municipalidad de Rosario, 1935), pp. 11-12, quoted in Cecilia Inés Galimberti, 'Planificar el territorio metropolitano', Revista de historia americana y argentina 51:1 (2016); the memoria is coauthored with Farengo and Guido and is not his sole writing
stops.campa: Six years after the ordinance, Rosario approves the Plan Regulador y de Extensión. The memoria that accompanies it reads the city as a product of its traffic before it prescribes anything, and it divides the river frontage by function so that each activity has its own determined ground along the Paraná. The northern zone is set aside as woodland reserve and declared fit for immediate use. Three men sign the memoria: della Paolera, Farengo and Guido.
stops.quote: El desarrollo vertiginoso de Rosario en estas últimas décadas, es la consecuencia de una concentración de actividades encauzadas por sus importantes vías de tráfico.
stops.quote_source: Carlos María della Paolera, Adolfo P. Farengo and Ángel Guido, Plan Regulador y de Extensión de Rosario, Memoria descriptiva y justificativa (Municipalidad de Rosario, 1935), p.11, quoted in Galimberti (2016)
suggested_refs: Plan Regulador y de Extensión de Rosario, Memoria descriptiva y justificativa (1935)
sources: Cecilia Inés Galimberti, 'Planificar el territorio metropolitano', Revista de historia americana y argentina 51:1 (2016)

stops.name: Avenida 9 de Julio, the corridor he inherits
stops.date_confidence: the 1933 project is attested by es.wikipedia's article on the Avenida 9 de Julio, which gives the expropriation of entire blocks at 110 metres; the prehistory of 1889, 1895 and 1912 comes from the same article. The claim that he was first to propose expropriating the corridor is corrected here: the corridor was already authorised for expropriation in 1912 at 33 metres, and what was new in 1933 was taking the blocks whole. The quotation is journalistic and Infobae does not cite the original document, so its first source is untraced. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: The corridor is older than he is. Intendente Francisco Seeber proposes it around 1889; the council approves a route by the architect Buschiazzo in 1895; national law authorises expropriation in 1912 for an artery thirty-three metres wide; a widened north-south avenue runs through Joseph Bouvard's Nuevo Plano of 1909 and through the 1925 plan Forestier advised. All of it is inherited. What he proposes in 1933 is to take the blocks entire, a hundred and ten metres across, leaving no remnant buildings standing, and to plant the ground that opens up. He is quoted calling it el verdadero desahogo del centro de Buenos Aires.
stops.quote: el verdadero desahogo del centro de Buenos Aires
stops.quote_source: attributed to Carlos María della Paolera in Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio: un ancho increíble, un obelisco por una fuente y el sueño de su creador' (16 November 2022); the article names no original document
suggested_refs: The 1909 Nuevo Plano commission and the 1925 Proyecto Orgánico, earlier drafts of the same corridor
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio...' (16 November 2022)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the variant of 1934
stops.date_confidence: attested by es.wikipedia's article on the Avenida 9 de Julio for a 1934 variant creating one centre of government buildings at the crossing with the Avenida de Mayo. The dossier's plural, government-building centres at major intersections, is corrected to the single node the source describes, and its rapid-transit streets are not in the source at all. His later rejection of ministries along the avenue is from Infobae. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: A year on he presents a variant: one centre of government buildings where the avenue crosses the Avenida de Mayo, the two great axes meeting at a single civic node. He abandons it. The civic centre he drew in 1934 is never mentioned by him again in anything reached. What he argues afterwards is the opposite, decentralisation, the ministries pushed off the avenue rather than gathered onto it, and when a sixty-metre block for social development is planned in the middle of the corridor he objects to it in one word: rascacielos.
suggested_refs: The 1934 variant plan for a government centre at 9 de Julio and Avenida de Mayo
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio...' (16 November 2022)

stops.name: Plaza de la República, the fountain that was not built
stops.date_confidence: the opposition to the obelisk and the fountain he had designed for the site are attested by Infobae (16 November 2022). The church of San Nicolás de Bari was demolished in 1931 for the widening of the Diagonal Norte, per es.wikipedia, so it was already gone before the 1933 project and cannot have been cleared by it; the dossier's account is corrected accordingly. The public auction of the demolition rubble is attested verbatim in the same Infobae piece. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: At the crossing of Corrientes the city raises an obelisk of white concrete on ground where the church of San Nicolás de Bari had stood until it was pulled down five years earlier for a different avenue. He had drawn a fountain for this spot: water at the crossing of the two axes, not a shaft. The obelisk goes up instead, becomes the sign of the city, and in time the sign of the avenue he is credited with creating. He loses that argument. Who overruled him, and on what grounds, nothing reached records.
suggested_refs: The Obelisco of Buenos Aires, raised 1936 on the cleared site of the church of San Nicolás de Bari
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio...' (16 November 2022)
es.wikipedia.org, 'Iglesia de San Nicolás de Bari'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the demolitions begin
stops.date_confidence: the 20 April 1937 start of demolitions, the 8 May opening of formal expropriation proceedings, and the 1 July start of construction under Federico Zamboni with the quantities of cement, iron and stone are all attested by es.wikipedia's article on the Avenida 9 de Julio. The dossier's roughly forty days of clearing is dropped: it appears in no source located, and the 31-day figure in circulation belongs to the Obelisco's construction in 1936. Infobae gives 138 properties, with 33 manzanas, correcting the dossier's 13 blocks
stops.campa: On the twentieth of April the wrecking starts: thirty-three blocks, a hundred and thirty-eight properties in the first phase, Frank Brown's circus, the Teatro del Pueblo, the Vieytes soap works. The municipal legal department opens formal expropriation proceedings eighteen days after the walls begin coming down, in that order. On the first of July construction proper begins under the engineer Federico Zamboni, with ten thousand tons of cement, three thousand tons of iron and forty thousand cubic metres of stone. The rubble is sold at public auction.
suggested_refs: The municipal expropriation file of 8 May 1937 for the 9 de Julio corridor
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio...' (16 November 2022)

stops.name: Avenida 9 de Julio, five hundred metres opened
stops.date_confidence: attested by es.wikipedia's article on the Avenida 9 de Julio: President Agustín P. Justo inaugurated a 500-metre stretch between Bartolomé Mitre and Viamonte on 12 October 1937. The dossier described the section as running Cerrito to Carlos Pellegrini, which is impossible, those being the two lateral roadways flanking the avenue rather than points along it; the pin is centred on the opened stretch
stops.campa: President Agustín P. Justo opens the first stretch, five hundred metres between Bartolomé Mitre and Viamonte, running past the new obelisk. It is a fraction of the corridor and it is enough to settle the argument about width: what is being built is a park with a road inside it, not a street with buildings on both sides. Two blocks of it are open and the rest is still buildings. The section from Mitre south to Belgrano is finished between 1944 and 1947.
suggested_refs: Press coverage of the inauguration of 12 October 1937

stops.name: Junín, the railway corridor turned avenue
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Avenida San Martín project at Junín with the engineer Rodolfo Henry is carried by the dossier and by es.wikipedia's list of his works for 1939, and was not independently reconfirmed; the description of the ramblas and the railway lands is dossier-only. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: In a pampa town cut in two by its railway, he works with the engineer Rodolfo Henry on the Avenida San Martín: the old railway lands turned into a planted avenue with ramblas down the middle, stitching the two halves of the grid back together. It is the same operation as the one in the capital at a hundredth of the scale, and unlike that one it is uncontested and quickly built. No study of the project has been located beyond the dossier's own account.
suggested_refs: The Avenida San Martín at Junín, on the lands of the former railway corridor

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Instituto Argentino de Urbanismo
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The founding of the Instituto Argentino de Urbanismo and the 1942 volume with Miguel Roca are dossier-only and were corroborated by nothing fetched. The founding venue was not located, so the pin is the canonical city point. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: With colleagues he founds the Instituto Argentino de Urbanismo, a professional and teaching body standing outside both the university and the municipality, on the reasoning that a discipline needs ground no intendente can take away from it. He has now built the discipline three times over: a chair, a municipal office, and a society, each one able to survive the loss of the others. Three years later he publishes with Miguel Roca an institutional volume, Buenos Aires. Una obra de progreso al servicio de la nación. Where the founding meeting was held has not been established.
suggested_refs: Carlos María della Paolera and Miguel Roca, Buenos Aires. Una obra de progreso al servicio de la nación (1942)

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, traffic, open space and the height of buildings
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Only the bibliographic listing of a Portuguese-language presentation, Tráfego, espaços livres e altura dos edificios, was located; the venue within Rio was not identified and personal travel is not established. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: He presents in Portuguese, in Rio de Janeiro, on traffic, open space and the height of buildings: the three quantities his whole practice weighs against each other, since every storey added to a building is traffic added to a street and open ground taken from somewhere else. Only the bibliographic listing of the paper survives, and whether he crossed to read it himself is not established. Brazil at this moment is driving the Avenida Presidente Vargas through the centre of Rio, clearing everything in its line.
suggested_refs: Tráfego, espaços livres e altura dos edificios, Rio de Janeiro, 1939

stops.name: Mendoza, the railways of a province
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The 1941 proposal for Mendoza and the 1943 study Reorganización del sistema ferroviario de Mendoza with Adolfo Farengo are dossier-only. Whether he travelled west or worked from Buenos Aires is not established. Coordinates corrected: OSM gives the city of Mendoza some 1.6 km west of the pair the dossier carried, which fell outside the centre. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: With Adolfo Farengo, the engineer of the Rosario plan, he produces a study on reorganising the railway system of Mendoza, two years after a proposal for the city itself. Mendoza is a wine capital rebuilt on a grid after an earthquake levelled it in 1861, its plazas laid out as refuges and its water run in acequias along every street, a city that already thinks about disaster and about irrigation. Whether he went west to see it, or worked from Buenos Aires off maps and timetables, the sources do not say.
suggested_refs: Carlos María della Paolera and Adolfo Farengo, Reorganización del sistema ferroviario de Mendoza (1943)

stops.name: La Plata, a civic centre for a city already drawn
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The proposal of a Gran Centro Cívico for La Plata in 1944 is dossier-only and no further detail was located; it was not built in the form proposed. Month and day default to 01, and the pin is Plaza Moreno, the centre of the 1882 plan
stops.campa: He proposes a Gran Centro Cívico for La Plata, a city drawn whole in 1882 before anybody lived in it: five kilometres square, diagonals cut across a grid, its public buildings ranged along an axis from the port to the woods, a plaza set at every six blocks. What he drew was not built in the form he proposed, and nothing further about it has been found. To be asked for a civic centre in the one Argentine city that was planned entire before it existed is a peculiar commission.
suggested_refs: Pedro Benoit's 1882 founding plan of La Plata, the design his centre would have been inserted into

stops.name: Bañado de Flores, the great park of the south
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The survey and the sanitation and park proposal for a Gran Parque del Sur in the Bañado de Flores are dossier-only; the area was partly built out later, but not as a single plan of his. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: South of the centre, on low ground that floods, the Bañado de Flores has been in turn a swamp, a rubbish tip and a place to put whatever the northern districts refuse. He surveys it and proposes a Gran Parque del Sur, drainage and sanitation first and park afterwards, the two treated as one operation rather than as a public work followed by an amenity. Parts of that ground become parkland later, under other names and other hands. No single plan of his was built here.
suggested_refs: The later Parque Almirante Brown, built over part of the Bañado de Flores

stops.name: Manzana de las Luces, the Instituto Superior de Urbanismo created
stops.date_confidence: attested and verified directly at isu.fadu.uba.ar/?p=29: a resolution of 11 March 1948 creating the Instituto Superior de Urbanismo de la Facultad de Arquitectura y Urbanismo. The pin is the downtown block where architecture teaching had sat since the previous century, the new faculty not yet having moved to Ciudad Universitaria; the 1948 premises are not confirmed by the institute's own page
stops.campa: By resolution of the eleventh of March the university creates an Instituto Superior de Urbanismo inside its Faculty of Architecture and Urbanism, a faculty itself only months old. Architecture had been taught in Buenos Aires inside the faculty of exact sciences since the previous century, and urbanism inside nothing at all. What he introduced as a lecture course at Rosario nineteen years earlier now has an institute, a faculty above it and a line in the budget. He is fifty-seven.
suggested_refs: Resolución del 11 de marzo de 1948, creating the Instituto Superior de Urbanismo, UBA

stops.name: Manzana de las Luces, named its first director
stops.date_confidence: attested and verified directly at isu.fadu.uba.ar/?p=29, whose record reads Resolución del 24 de abril de 1948: Director Profesor Ingeniero Carlos M. Della Paolera. That Gaston Bardet gave the inaugural lectures comes from iaa.fadu.uba.ar/ojs article 264. The 1948 premises of the faculty are not confirmed and the pin follows the previous stop
stops.campa: A second resolution, six weeks after the first, names the director. The inaugural lectures are given by Gaston Bardet, French urbanist and son-in-law of Marcel Poëte, so the institute opens with the voice of the Paris school in the room, twenty years after the Argentine student walked out of it with a diploma nobody in his country could read. The institute's own chronology keeps the appointment in one line: Resolución del 24 de abril de 1948: Director Profesor Ingeniero Carlos M. Della Paolera.
suggested_refs: Resolución del 24 de abril de 1948 naming the first director of the ISU

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a day for the whole profession
stops.date_confidence: the 1949 proposal is attested by iaa.fadu.uba.ar/ojs article 264, which dates the first observance to 1950. The dossier claims a first observance in 1949 and es.wikipedia credits him as creator without separating the 1934 symbol from the later day. That contradiction between sources is flagged and not resolved. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: He proposes an annual world day of urbanism fixed to the eighth of November, with his 1934 symbol as its mark: an instrument for making a scattered profession visible to itself and to the public on one date every year. The proposal goes out through the international planning bodies and not through any government. He is fifty-nine, long out of the municipal office, and what he reaches for now is neither a plan nor a law but a calendar. It is kept today in more than thirty countries.
suggested_refs: The 8 November observance as maintained by ISOCARP and the Royal Town Planning Institute

stops.name: Ezeiza, the airport and the region
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Only a bibliographic listing of L'Aéroport National du Grand Buenos Aires was located; the study is not established as the design basis of the airport, and the pin marks the airfield as the nearest identifiable landmark to the study's subject rather than a place he is recorded at. Month and day default to 01
stops.campa: He writes on the national airport of Greater Buenos Aires. The field at Ezeiza, thirty kilometres out on the pampa, has been open three years and is the largest in South America; Only a bibliographic listing of the paper was located, and nothing establishes it as the basis of anything built out there. What interests him is what an airport does to a region, the roads dragged after it and the settlement seeded around it, at a metropolitan scale no municipal plan was drawn for.
suggested_refs: Carlos María della Paolera, L'Aéroport National du Grand Buenos Aires (c. 1950)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the directorship ends
stops.date_confidence: attested, against the dossier's own doubt: isu.fadu.uba.ar/?p=29 records a Resolución del 28 de septiembre de 1956 installing Arq. Sergio Fernández Pico as Director, which a previous reading of the same page missed. Nothing on the page frames the change as punitive and nothing explains it. The location of the faculty in 1956 was not established here and the pin follows the earlier institute stops
stops.campa: By resolution of the twenty-eighth of September the architect Sergio Fernández Pico is installed as director of the institute. Della Paolera is sixty-six. Nothing in the record frames the change as a dismissal and nothing explains it; the resolution names a successor, and that is the whole of what it does. Argentina in 1956 is a year past a coup and its universities are being reorganised. Whether the two facts touch each other, no paper reached will say.
suggested_refs: The resolution of 28 September 1956, ISU directorship

segments.name: Afterward: the Name on the Street

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the death
stops.date_confidence: attested for 15 September 1960 in Buenos Aires by es.wikipedia, which gives his age as 70; Infobae carries only the year. No source located gives a cause of death, a hospital, or a burial place, and the silence is reported here as the current state of the record rather than as a finding. The pin is the canonical city point
stops.campa: He dies on the fifteenth of September, eight days after his seventieth birthday. Cause of death, hospital, funeral, cemetery: on every one of these the record reached is silent, and the silence is evidence of nothing except that nobody wrote it down. The avenue he reconceived is open through the centre and driven to neither end of the city. The chair at Rosario, the chair at Buenos Aires, the municipal office, the institute and the day in November are all still standing.
suggested_refs: Burial and cemetery records for Buenos Aires, September 1960, not located
sources: Infobae, 'El origen de la 9 de Julio...' (16 November 2022)

stops.name: Sociedad Central de Arquitectos, the papers gathered
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The deposit of his plans and papers with the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos and the Museo de la Ciudad is dossier-only and undated; 1961 is an ordering device with no source behind it. The 1977 anthology is confirmed as an edition by Open Library, though Randle's editorship and the Oikos imprint appear only in the dossier's bibliography. The quotation is verified verbatim in the Télam wire story, whose date is 7 November 2022 and not 2021 as the dossier had it. Coordinates corrected by some 350 m to the OSM figure
stops.campa: His plans, drawings and professional papers go to the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos and to the Museo de la Ciudad, split across two deposits. In 1977 Patricio Randle selects an anthology of his writing, Buenos Aires y sus problemas urbanos, which remains the only collected edition of his own words. Sixty years after the death the work of gathering the rest falls to a grandson who never met him, the economic historian Gerardo della Paolera, working from what the family had kept as talk.
stops.quote: La idea surgió porque no conocía a mi abuelo, había toda una tradición oral en nuestra familia.
stops.quote_source: Gerardo della Paolera, Agencia Télam wire story, reproduced at grupolaprovincia.com, 7 November 2022, on the presentation of the CEDODAL monograph edited by Ramón Gutiérrez
suggested_refs: Carlos M. della Paolera, Buenos Aires y sus problemas urbanos (1977)
Ramón Gutiérrez, ed., Carlos María Della Paolera y el urbanismo científico en la Argentina (CEDODAL, 2021)
sources: Open Library record for Buenos Aires y sus problemas urbanos (1977)
Web crawl dossier for the deposit itself

stops.name: Retiro, the street in Catalinas Norte
stops.date_confidence: the street and the plazoleta are attested by direct OpenStreetMap/Nominatim query, way 83432713 for Calle Carlos M. Della Paolera in Catalinas Norte and way 114352739 for the Plazoleta Carlos María Della Paolera in Retiro; neither appears in the dossier. No naming date was established for either, and 1980 is an ordering device with no source behind it
stops.campa: In Catalinas Norte, the office district raised on filled port land north of the centre, three short segments of street carry the name Carlos M. Della Paolera, and a few blocks away a small triangle of pavement and planting is the Plazoleta Carlos María Della Paolera. Both sit in the part of Buenos Aires most thoroughly made by the kind of large-scale replanning he spent his life arguing for. When the names were voted, and by whom, has not been established.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires municipal street-naming ordinances for Catalinas Norte and Retiro

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the avenue and the plazoleta of urbanism
stops.date_confidence: attested by OpenStreetMap query: Avenida Ingeniero Della Paolera runs through several Mar del Plata barrios, and a Plazoleta Ing. Carlos María Della Paolera del Urbanismo stands in La Perla at -37.9865583, -57.5448035. Spanish Wikipedia mentions a Mar del Plata street without detail, understating both. No naming date was found and 1980 is an ordering device only; the pin is the centre point of the avenue
stops.campa: The coast city he lectured in remembers him at length. An Avenida Ingeniero Della Paolera runs through Aeroparque, Los Pinares, Parque Montemar, López de Gomara and Caisamar y Estrada, and in La Perla there is a Plazoleta Ing. Carlos María della Paolera. No document reached says when the council voted either name. The naming is more generous than anything the capital gave him, and it comes from a city that adopted none of his proposals. The municipality subtitles the plazoleta del Urbanismo, as though the man and the discipline were interchangeable on a street sign.
suggested_refs: Mar del Plata street register, Avenida Ingeniero Della Paolera and Plazoleta del Urbanismo, La Perla
sources: OpenStreetMap/Nominatim, Mar del Plata street query

stops.name: São Paulo, the street the reference works put in Rio
stops.date_confidence: attested by an OpenStreetMap country-wide query for Della Paolera in Brazil, which returns Rua Carlos Maria Della Paolera in Jardim da Saúde, Cursino, São Paulo, and returns nothing at all in Rio de Janeiro or Tijuca. The Tijuca claim in es.wikipedia is unsourced in the article itself and is corrected here rather than repeated. No naming date was found and 1980 is an ordering device only
stops.campa: In Jardim da Saúde, in the Cursino district on the southern side of São Paulo, a Rua Carlos Maria Della Paolera runs between two blocks of low houses, a residential street of no consequence in a district he never wrote about. The reference works that mention a Brazilian street for him place it in Tijuca, in Rio de Janeiro, where a search of the whole Brazilian street register turns up nothing of the kind. The commemoration is real. Every account of it names the wrong city, and none of them says who proposed the name.
suggested_refs: São Paulo municipal street register, Jardim da Saúde, CEP 04150-000
sources: OpenStreetMap/Nominatim, Brazil-wide query for Della Paolera
es.wikipedia.org, 'Carlos María della Paolera' (unsourced Tijuca claim, corrected)

stops.name: Ciudad Universitaria, the institute takes his name
stops.date_confidence: attested at isu.fadu.uba.ar/?p=29: Resolución (CD) 579 of 16 December 2003 adopting the name Instituto Superior de Urbanismo, Territorio y el Ambiente. The same page dates the end of the institute's dormancy to Resolución 321 (CD) of 7 December 1993, appointing Juan Manuel Borthagaray as director; it gives no start year for the dormancy, so the dossier's 1980-1994 span is not asserted here. Coordinates are the OSM figure for FADU at Ciudad Universitaria, Intendente Güiraldes 2160
stops.campa: By resolution 579 of the faculty council the institute is renamed Instituto Superior de Urbanismo, Territorio y el Ambiente Carlos María della Paolera. It had lain dormant for years and was brought back at the end of 1993 with Juan Manuel Borthagaray appointed to direct it. The faculty by then sits out at Ciudad Universitaria on the river, concrete pavilions standing on landfill, several kilometres and one whole conception of the city away from the colonial block downtown where the institute was created in 1948.
suggested_refs: Resolución (CD) 579 of 16 December 2003, Facultad de Arquitectura, Diseño y Urbanismo, UBA
